'''Horst Feistel''' (January 30, 1915<ref>Both (Diffie and Landau, 1998), and (Levy, 2001) give Feistel's birth year as 1914. The dates included here are based on the genealogical notes.</ref> – November 14, 1990<ref name=":0" />) was a German-American [[cryptographer]] who worked on the design of [[ciphers]] at [[IBM]], initiating research that culminated in the development of the [[Data Encryption Standard]] (DES) in the 1970s. The structure used in DES, called a [[Feistel network]], is commonly used in many [[block ciphers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.cs.du.edu/~ramki/courses/security/2011Winter/notes/feistelProof.pdf|title=Block ciphers|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111125070623/https://web.cs.du.edu/~ramki/courses/security/2011Winter/notes/feistelProof.pdf |archive-date=2011-11-25 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.cs.ucdavis.edu/~rogaway/papers/feistel.pdf|title= On Generalized Feistel networks}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cs.umd.edu/~gasarch/COURSES/456/F18/lecbc3/lecbc3.pdf|title=Feistel networks}}</ref>

==Life and work==
Feistel was born in [[Berlin]], [[Germany]] in 1915, and moved to the [[United States]] in 1934. During [[World War II]], he was placed under house arrest, but gained US citizenship on 31 January 1944. The following day he was granted a security clearance and began work for the US [[Air Force Cambridge Research Center]] (AFCRC) on [[Identification Friend or Foe]] (IFF) devices until the 1950s. He was subsequently employed at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]]'s [[Lincoln Laboratory]], then the [[MITRE]] corporation. In 1968, Feistel became a Research Staff Member at the [[IBM]] [[Thomas J. Watson Research Center|T.J Watson Center]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Konheim |first=Alan G. |date=2019 |title=Horst Feistel: the inventor of LUCIFER, the cryptographic algorithm that changed cryptology |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s13389-018-0198-5 |journal=Journal of Cryptographic Engineering |language=en |volume=9 |issue=1 |pages=85–100 |doi=10.1007/s13389-018-0198-5 |issn=2190-8508|url-access=subscription }}</ref> During his time there he received an award for his cryptographic work. In 1971, he patented the [[block cipher]] [[Cryptosystem|cryptographic system]] at IBM.<ref name=":0" /> His research at [[IBM]] led to the development of the [[Lucifer (cipher)|Lucifer]] and [[Data Encryption Standard]] (DES) ciphers. Feistel was one of the earliest non-government researchers to study the design and theory of [[block cipher]]s.

Feistel lent his name to the [[Feistel network]] construction, a common method for constructing block ciphers (for example DES).

Feistel obtained a [[bachelor's degree]] at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], and his [[master's degree|master's]] at [[Harvard]], both in [[physics]]. He married Leona (Gage) in 1945, with whom he had a daughter, Peggy.
